alignments.note: Inferential conjunction rendered by the single word *Wherefore*.
Participle rendered by the bare participle *receiving*; the ASV fronts it, which rule 15 permits.
The Greek is anarthrous, so no article competes and the supplied *a* is an ordinary rule 7/51 helper on the noun it determines.

Privative adjective recast as a finite relative clause; the relativizer, the modal and the copula are rule 7/9 helpers on it, and rule 84's principle keeps the head on the meaning-bearing *shaken*, *cannot be* spelling only the privative prefix.
Hortatory subjunctive: the supplied *let us* is the inflection's own helper under rules 7 and 9, and rule 17 heads on the lexical verb rather than the auxiliary.
The margin's *thankfulness* is an alternative rendering, not a second target token.
Portmanteau under rule 35: *where-* answers to the relative and *-by* to `διά`, so the pair is one `aligned` unit headed on the pronominal, not `noncompositional` under rule 45.

Support-verb rendering of one Greek verb: rules 17 and 91 head on the meaning-bearing complement *service*, the corpus spending *offer* on no part of `λατρεύω`; the subject and modal ride along under rules 7 and 9.
Rule 104's `εὐ-` family: the stem word carries the lexeme, so the head is *pleasing* and not *well*.
The ASV gives `θεῷ` no determiner, so the article has no *the* to anchor and is `unrepresented` under rule 23; rule 21 forbids leaving a bare *to* on it, so the case preposition stays with the noun.
The dative's case preposition rides with the noun, the article having no determiner to anchor it (rules 21, 23).
The margin's *godly fear* is an alternative rendering, not a second target token.
Expressed conjunction joining the two genitives.

review_notes: All 16 source and 25 target ids partitioned exactly once.
`δι᾽ ἧς` → *whereby* taken as rule 35 `aligned` rather than rule 45 `noncompositional`, since *-by* answers to the preposition; the competing reading would be a fused unit with null heads.
`λατρεύωμεν` → *may offer service* headed on *service* under rule 91's operational test; heading on *offer* would rest only on English syntax, which rule 17 refuses.
